dossiers.catalyst_stack: On 2026-07-22 Alphabet delivered a massive Q2 2026 beat (EPS $9.11 vs ~$2.88 consensus, revenue $119.80B) with Google Cloud up 82% YoY to $24.77B and a $514B backlog, but raised 2026 capex to $195-205B, pressuring shares. On 2026-09-02 a judge allowed Google to keep its advertising business despite the ad tech monopoly ruling, a major favorable legal catalyst, while the 2026-07-02 EU court upheld a €4.1B antitrust fine and 2026-07-23 added a $1B EU fine. Strategic AI momentum continued with the 2026-08-24 Verizon Gemini Enterprise partnership, the 2026-09-08 Accenture Gemini Enterprise business group, and the 2026-05-18 Blackstone $5B TPU cloud JV. Offsetting risks include the 2026-04-25 search monopoly remedies barring exclusive distribution deals, the 2026-10-01 €640M ad tech damages claim, and the 2026-08-31 social media addiction negligence finding.
dossiers.key_assumption: The favorable 2026-09-02 ad tech ruling (Google keeps its ad business) and the Q2 2026 earnings/cloud acceleration outweigh the cumulative antitrust fines and capex-driven margin pressure, so the net catalyst balance remains positive.

dossiers.catalyst_stack: On 2026-07-22, Alphabet posted better-than-expected Q2 CY2026 sales with Google Cloud growth accelerating, though shares slipped on a capex surge and earnings-quality questions surfaced by 2026-07-24. On 2026-09-09, Google announced a two-year €13 billion AI infrastructure investment in Finland, reinforcing its capacity expansion and cloud/AI demand narrative. On 2026-08-19, Google struck an AI chip deal with Marvell allowing up to $12.2 billion in share purchases, and on 2026-07-30 Oracle agreed to make Gemini models available to thousands of enterprise customers. Offsetting these positives, on 2026-07-02 Google lost its appeal against a record €4.1 billion EU antitrust fine and on 2026-07-01 was hit with a $2 billion antitrust judgment for skewing shopping searches, keeping regulatory risk elevated.
dossiers.key_assumption: The AI/cloud growth catalysts (Finland capex, Marvell chip deal, Oracle Gemini distribution, Q2 Cloud acceleration) outweigh the EU antitrust fine and shopping-search judgment, and no further binary antitrust remedy (e.g., Chrome divestiture or DMA structural penalty) materializes in the near term.

dossiers.catalyst_stack: On 2026-04-23 and 2026-07-26, Baker Hughes delivered Q1 and Q2 beats with adjusted EBITDA of $1.16B and $1.23B, record IET orders of $7.1B, and $1.1B free cash flow. On 2026-07-10 and 2026-07-16, the company cleared conditional EU antitrust approval and completed the $13.6B Chart Industries acquisition, then raised 2026 revenue guidance to $28.5B-$30.3B on 2026-09-09. Contract momentum accelerated with bp North Sea stimulation on 2026-09-04, Venture Global LNG orders on 2026-09-13, and Venezuela gas infrastructure agreements on 2026-10-05. Offsetting this, on 2026-09-10 the stock fell 6.7% after management flagged near-term margin and FCF pressure from Chart, cutting 2026 FCF conversion to 40%-45%, while Jefferies trimmed its target to $77 on 2026-09-28.
dossiers.key_assumption: Chart Industries integration proceeds broadly on plan and the 2026 guidance raise is not derailed by margin/FCF pressure or further regulatory/geopolitical shocks.
